text:
incident-bot: Pager: serve-runtime HIGH — multiple pods on gpu-node-37 reporting Evicted/CrashLoopBackOff due to ephemeral storage pressure. Auto-escalating to oncall.
Alex H: seeing a cascade — model-cache pods OOM + eviction across 3 pods on node-37, then kubelet evicted more due to ephemeral-writeback.
Priya S: verified: /var/lib/modelcache on the node is at 98% and journald is spiking. Logs show constant checkpoint writes from modelcache v2.3.1.
Jamie (ops): stack trace from one runtime container: 
```
[2026-03-15T09:12:23Z] cuda: driver timeout, killing container (CUDA_ERROR_ILLEGAL_ADDRESS)
[2026-03-15T09:12:24Z] oom-killer: kill process 2345 (runtime) score 987 or sacrifice child
[2026-03-15T09:12:24Z] eviction: pod "modelcache-7f9" deleted due to ephemeral-storage
```
Alex H: customer impact: a handful of requests to hosted endpoints 1) increased latency 2) 503s while failover to other region happened. Support reported two paying customers with degraded throughput.
Katherine (SRE): corroborating tracing — prefix cache miss rate spiked when modelcache pods were evicted, causing backend fallback to cold-start model loads which amplified disk writes.
deploy-bot: deploy 3860011100 started for modelcache-v2.3.1-rollout at 09:05Z — partial rollout to node-37.
Priya S: oh nice, that rollout likely wrote new cache checkpoints concurrently with existing heavy model loads. Could be double-writing checkpoints.
Jamie (ops): immediate mitigations: 1) cordon gpu-node-37 2) scale modelcache down to 0 on that node (taint/affinity) 3) delete large old checkpoints <command>
Lee: running commands now: 
```sh
kubectl cordon gpu-node-37
kubectl get pods -o wide | grep modelcache
kubectl delete pod modelcache-7f9 --namespace=serve-runtime
```
logs-bot: pulled last 5k lines from modelcache-7f9: repeated "checkpoint write failed: no space left on device" and "corrupt header detected: magic mismatch" entries.
Alex H: corruption msg worries me — if checkpoints are half-written, next restart tries to read corrupted metadata and OOMs. Need to stop restarts on those pods until we clean.
Marta: I'm taking handoff in 10m; do we have a short-run mitigation we can leave?
Priya S: yes — set modelcache env var to READ_ONLY=true for nodes in the pool so they don't try to write checkpoints during recovery. Also disable aggressive log-levels for that service.
Jamie (ops): applied a temporary patch to the DaemonSet to set READ_ONLY=true and LOG_LEVEL=warn for modelcache-serve. Rolling update in progress.
deploy-bot: patch applied: modelcache-daemonset updated — rolling restart initiated (grace period 60s).
Katherine (SRE): we should also shrink journald retention and rotate to avoid journal flooding. Running 
```sh
journalctl --vacuum-time=2d
systemctl restart systemd-journald
```
Lee: ran vacuum, freed ~12GB on node-37. Ephemeral went from 98% -> 82%. Kernel stopped evicting but some pods still crash because of previous corruption.
Alex H: plan for next hour: 1) quarantine node-37 2) run checkpoint repair script to move corrupted files to /tmp for later analysis 3) restore modelcache from last known-good snapshot 4) monitor tail latency and error budget.
Priya S: checkpoint repair script: 
```sh
for f in /var/lib/modelcache/checkpoints/*.chk; do 
  if ! modelcache-verify $f; then mv $f /tmp/corrupt-$(basename $f); fi
done
```
Jamie (ops): started snapshot restore of modelcache from s3://redwood-backups/serve-runtime/modelcache/2026-03-15-08-55.tar.gz to node-38.
support-bot: Support: notfied impacted customers A & B at 09:40Z with temporary mitigation notes. Status page updated: partial degradation in US-west-2.
Alex H: can we get a short RCA pointer ASAP: double checkpoint writes + journald growth caused disk saturation which triggered kubelet evictions; CUDA-driver timeouts and OOMs were downstream.
Marta: I'm oncall now. I'll keep node-37 cordoned and watch the repair/restore. If we see any other nodes trending >85% ephemeral, we'll preemptively drain them.
Katherine (SRE): recommend follow-ups: 1) add a pre-deploy hook to throttle checkpoint writes during rollout, 2) add eviction-aware checkpointing (write to mounted PV with quota), 3) add alert for journalctl bytes growth per node.
Lee: filing infra ticket INF-2026-119 to request larger ephemeral volumes on gpu-backed fleets for heavy-model workloads.
Priya S: leaving one more note — there were a couple of CUDA driver error lines that match a known upstream bug in CUDA 12.2 kernels under heavy IO; filing bug with runtime team.
Marta: handoff checklist: I have watch, ongoing restore tracked, customers notified, node cordoned, READ_ONLY set. If anything spikes I will page the SRE runbook.
Alex H: thanks all. tagging for postmortem owners: @Katherine (SRE) to lead RCA, @Priya S for modelcache mitigation plan, @Lee for infra ticket.
incident-bot: Incident status updated: MEDIUM -> ACTIVE -> Mitigating; sla_impact: partial. Next update expected in 30m.
